2. Heard Sri Manish Kumar, learned counsel for the applicants, Sri Ankit Srivastava, learned counsel for the State and perused the records.
3.
As per officer report dated 20.5.2023 a report from concerned court has been received which is dated 15.5.2023 wherein it has been stated that the compromise has been verified.

3. The present application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicants Sonu Idrishi,
Sameena, Islammuddeen @ Kalla Master, Sarfraj, Paley Khan with the prayer to quash the entire Sonu Idrishi And 4 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33045076/

323, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 D.P. Act 1961, P.S. Mahila Thana, District Meerut and the impugned charge sheet no. 55 of 2020, dated 9.10.2020 in Criminal Case No. 1618 of 2021, Case Crime No. 56 of 2020, u/s 498A, 323, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 D.P. Act 1961, P.S. Mahila Thana, District Meerut and with the further prayer to stay the entire further proceedings of said case pending before the Fast Track Court (C.A.W.) (JD), Meerut.

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the parties have settled the dispute amicably out of court and on the basis of compromise the present Criminal Misc. Application U/S 482 Cr.P.C. has been before this Court in which an order for verification of the compromise was passed on 13.4.2023.

It is argued that in compliance of the order dated 13.4.2023 of this Court, the parties have filed the said compromise application along with affidavit and the order of this Court before the concerned court for its verification after which the concerned court has verified the said compromise vide its order dated 09.5.2023, copy of which is on record.

It is argued that the opposite party no. 2 is not interested to pursue the matter pending in the trial court and is not inclined to give any evidence against the applicants and therefore the impugned proceedings be quashed on the ground of compromise between the parties.
5. Learned State counsel could not dispute the factum of compromise which was duly verified by the concerned trial court.

6. The law with regards to quashing of a case on the basis of settlement arrived between the parties,
is well settled.

The Apex Court in the cases of (1) B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and another: (2003)4 SCC 675; (2) Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation : (2008) 9 SCC 677; (3) Manoj Sharma Vs. State and others: ( 2008) 16 SCC 1; (4) Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab:
(2012) 10 SCC 303; (5) Shaifullah and others Vs. State of U.P. And another: 2013 (83) ACC 278 and (6) Parbatbhai Ahir@Parbatbhai @ Bhimsinbhai Karmur and others Vs. State of Gujarat and another: (2017) 9 SCC 641 has held that the cases in which the parties have settled their grievances can be quashed.
7. From perusal of the records and the law laid down by the Apex Court on the subject matter, the present case is a good case for exercising powers by this Court to quash the proceedings and the charge sheet as prayed for by the applicants.
